questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
During my exchange at UCLA, I took mostly undergraduate courses, which were generally easier than I expected. These courses often involved typical assignments, exams, and lectures, and the workload varied depending on the course. While some were quite manageable and didn’t challenge me too much, others required more time and effort, especially if they involved projects or group work. Overall, if you already have a strong foundation in the subject, the undergraduate courses are relatively accessible.

However, UCLA also offers the opportunity to take graduate courses, which would have raised the difficulty level significantly. Graduate courses are designed for more advanced students and often require a deeper understanding of the material. These courses are more challenging, with a greater emphasis on independent thinking, research, and analysis. You’re expected to engage in more critical discussions, tackle complex problems, and produce high-quality, in-depth work.

Additionally, if you were involved in research, that would also increase the level of difficulty. Research projects at UCLA are often cutting-edge and demand a lot of initiative, problem-solving, and critical thinking. While being involved in research would push you academically, it’s also an incredibly valuable learning experience. Whether you were contributing to an ongoing project or conducting your own, research at UCLA can be quite challenging but also rewarding for those interested in further academic pursuits or careers in research.
